CORAM: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE HANCHATE SANJEEVKUMAR  ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE HANCHATE SANJEEVKUMAR)

These appeals are preferred against the common judgment and award dated 09.06.2014 passed in MVC Nos.1999/12 and 2013/2012, on the file of Senior Civil Judge and Additional M.A.C.T, Bailhongal (for short,
'Tribunal').
2.

sentences.text: MFA No.103418/2014 and MFA No.100540/2015 are filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of compensation.

3. MFA No.102367/2014 is filed by the insurance company praying to reduce the quantum of compensation in MVC No.1999/2012 (MFA No.103418/2014).
4.
Heard the arguments and perused the material placed before the Court.
NC: 2025:KHC-D:131 5. The occurrence of accident, injuries sustained by the claimants, coverage of insurance are not in dispute in this case.

6. Brief facts leading to file these appeals are that on 20.11.2011, the appellant/claimant in MVC No.2013/2012 was proceeding on the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-24/L-1512 towards his village Avaradi from Dhavaleshwar.
At that time the appellant/claimant in MVC No.1999/12 was the pillion rider.
The petitioner in MVC No.2013/2012 was riding the Motorcycle in a moderate speed, after observing the road traffic rules on the left side of the road.

While going so, when they came near the bus- stand of Chinchakhindi K.D. village on Mudhol road within the limits of Lokapur Police station,
at that time at about 17-30 hours, the driver of Tractor Trailer bearing Reg.No.KA-28/A-4197 owned by respondent No.1 came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner in a high speed so as to endanger human life and dashed against KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-23/F-625 and then NC: 2025:KHC-D:131 dashed to another vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-29/A-3952 and finally dashed to the motorcycle of the petitioners and thereby caused accident.
7. In the present case, all particulars on record have proved that the claimant has suffered following injuries.
i. Right eye echymosis present.
ii. CLW over right supra orbital region.
iii. Comminuted fracture lateral wall of right orbit bone.

In this case, the tribunal has awarded compensation under various heads as under:
SL.NO. PARTICULARS AMOUNT (IN.RS.)
1. Pain and suffering 50,000/-

2 . Loss of amenities and future 20,000/-
unhappiness 3.

Medical expenses incurred 20,000/-
4. Incidental expenses 10,000/-
5. Loss of income during laid up and 5,000/-
rest period 6. Loss of future income 2,70,000/-
7.

Future medical expenses --- Total Compensation 3,75,000/-
9.
The quantum of compensation awarded under the head loss of future income is on lesser side.

Since the NC: 2025:KHC-D:131 notional income adopted is on lesser side,
therefore, on this head, claimant is entitled to adequate compensation and on other heads, the quantum of compensation awarded is correct.
10. PW-3 and 4 who are Doctor and Orthopedic surgeon have stated that the claimant has suffered loss of 30% of eye vision and also due to comminuted fracture lateral wall of the right orbit bone, the claimant has suffered disability to the extent of 25%.

The Tribunal has taken 20% of permanent physical and functional disability by holding notional income at Rs.5,000/- per month and by adding 50% of income towards future prospectus, awarded compensation of Rs.2,70,000/- under the head loss of future earning due to disability.

The accident occurred on 20.11.2011,
therefore, notional income would be Rs.6,000/- per month as per the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
Since the claimant has suffered significant disability to the eyes and also suffered comminuted fracture.

Therefore, it is just NC: 2025:KHC-D:131 and proper to take 22% as functional disability and 40%
of income is to be added towards loss of future prospects in life but not 50%.
11. The claimant was aged 38 years at the time of accident.

Therefore, the appropriate multiplier is '15'.
Shridevi W/O Mallanagouda Patil vs Narayana S/O Namadev Sathe on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96591325/
5

Therefore, loss of future income due to disability is reassessed as under:
Rs.6000 + 40% x 12 x 15 x 22% = Rs.3,32,640/-
12.
Further, the quantum of compensation awarded under other heads by the tribunal is found to be correct.

Hence, the claimant is entitled for total compensation under various heads as under:
SL.NO. PARTICULARS AMOUNT (IN.RS.)
1. Pain and suffering 50,000 2. Loss of amenities and future 20,000 unhappiness 3.
Medical expenses incurred 20,000 4. Incidental expenses 10,000 5. Loss of income during laid up and 5,000 rest period 6. Loss of future income 3,32,640 7.
Future medical expenses ---  Total Compensation 4,37,640  NC: 2025:KHC-D:131 13.

Therefore, the claimant is entitled for total compensation of Rs.4,37,640/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till realization, as against Rs.3,75,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation within eight weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

14. In this case though the insurance company has contended that the claimant has not suffered disability, but on considering the Doctors evidence that the loss of 30%
of eye sight is significant one affecting the agricultural work of the claimant.
Just because, the fracture is of orbital bone, it cannot be said that the claimant has not suffered disability.
Agricultural work requires physical strength apart from the work home making in the home.
Therefore, the claimant has suffered significant disability.

sentences.text: 6 Hence, the appeal filed by the insurance company is liable to be dismissed.
In this case, from the medical evidence on record it is proved that the claimant had suffered the following injuries.
i. Tiny Hemorrhagic contusion over bilateral frontal region.
ii. Bleed noted in body of left lateral ventricle.

iii. CLW over left parietal region.
iv. CLW over right knee.
16.
The Tribunal has awarded global compensation of Rs.50,000/-.

Upon considering the claimant has spent Rs.15,773/- towards medical expenses and hospital charges, the claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation marginally considering the nature of injury sustained and medical expenses spent.

Therefore, it is just and proper to award additional global compensation of Rs.20,000/- in addition to what has been awarded by the tribunal, along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization.
. Therefore, the appeals filed by the claimants are liable to be allowed in part and the appeal filed by the insurance company is liable to be dismissed.

18. In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) MFA No.103418/2014 and 100540/2015 are allowed in part.
ii) MFA No.102367/2014 is dismissed.
iii) The judgment and awards dated 09.06.2014, passed by the Senior Civil Judge and Addl. M.A.C.T, Bailhongal, in MVC Nos.1999/12 and 2013/2012, stand modified.

iv) The claimant in MFA No.103418/2014 is entitled for total compensation of Rs.4,37,640/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization, as against the compensation of Rs.3,75,000/- awarded by the tribunal.
